rule: Code outside a method body: the caller is its location. Field/val initializer → `Type#field`; C# property accessor → `Type#Prop` (get) / `Type#Prop=` (set); Ruby setter → `Type#x=`; `static {}` block → `Type#<clinit>`. Non-lazy initializers also get an `implicit` edge from `<clinit>`/`<init>`; lazy ones do not. `implicit`: an execution edge the language runs without a written call — `Type#<clinit>` → `Type#field` (static initializer), `Type#<init>` → `Type#field` (instance field initializer). Line = the field's line. Top-level / file-level code (outside any function or type): the caller is the file's module ID. Languages with a module qualifier use it (Python module, JS/TS module, Lua module, OCaml/Haskell module, Rust module path `crate::a::b`, Groovy `pkg.Script#run`). Languages without one (Ruby, PHP, C, C++, ObjC, Zig file scope) use the file path below the scan root without extension (`lib/devise/rails/routes`). **Typed receivers (decision A) cover every declaration of the receiver's type**: locals, parameters, fields, and file-scope globals/statics (C, C++, ObjC, Zig, Rust `static`).
notes: 'int limit_ = init_count();' is a non-static (instance) field initializer: its call has caller Registry#limit_, and the field gets an implicit edge Registry#<init> → Registry#limit_ on the field's line (core/types.h:11). The implicit edge is high because both ends are defined in the scan (the tier rule; SPEC gives no separate tier for implicit). The file-scope initializers of g_count and g_reg (outside any function or type) have the file path below the scan root without extension as caller: 'core/registry'. g_reg is a file-scope global with declared type Registry* (Decisions 2026-10-29) → g_reg->add names Registry#add. ': cap_(cap)' initialises a scalar: not a call. The prototype 'int init_count();' is a declaration.
